findings.finding: ONDS is an equity-funded roll-up of defense/security hardware makers (drones, counter-UAS, ISR, precision-strike components) sold to governments by program and order: revenue = orders converted from backlog, by program (product 43.4M, service 23.6M, development 16.7M of Q2 2026 revenue 83.8M; 41% recognized over time). The KPIs are company-defined, not GAAP: backlog 613M reported / 757M pro forma at 2026-06-30 (68.3M at 2025-12-31), Q2 orders 175M (book-to-bill ~2.1x), 105M more Q3-to-date by 2026-08-10. GAAP RPO was only 0.47M at FY2025, so backlog conversion timing is unverified. No econ registry model fits (econ-review run: unclassified, not assessed; input_sha256 7e6b5ae2...): the identity is read by hand and no unit price or units KPI is disclosed.

Q2 2026 revenue grew 13.4x y/y (83.8M vs 6.3M; ln = 2.59). The company's pro forma same-portfolio growth is +85% (ln 0.62, ~24% of the log growth). The other ~76% (ln 1.98) is the acquisition perimeter (reclassification/bought, not organic). For FY2026 the 525-550M target equals '>30% pro forma organic growth' at the midpoint. That implies the current portfolio already had about 413M of revenue in FY2025 (537.5/1.30) against 50.7M reported, so about 360M of the step-up is bought revenue. Within the organic part, volume vs price vs wartime (Israel) demand cannot be separated from the disclosures: the residual is unexplained. Structural: orders and backlog build (book-to-bill 2.1x). Cyclical/conflict-driven: the Israeli share (45% of Q2 revenue). Macro: defense budgets. Mix: product mix after acquisitions (GAAP gross margin 53.1% Q2-25 -> 49.2% Q1-26 -> 43.1% Q2-26).

Government defense budgets fund the demand; no vendor financing or take-or-pay was found. Concentration is high: Customer A (unnamed; Israeli MOD is a hypothesis) was 40% of Q2 2026 revenue, 37% of H1 and 43% of receivables (73% of receivables at 2025-12-31); in FY2025 the top two customers were 55% and 11%. Israel was 60.8% of FY2025 and 44.7% of Q2 2026 revenue. Firm exposure vs contingent: the U.S. Army LUS IDIQ is a 982M CEILING with >240M of orders captured (~24% firm); the 140M combat-engineering-vehicles program starts volume deliveries in Q4 2026. Customer prepayments are modest (contract liabilities 29.7M, ~35% of one quarter's revenue).

Revenue guidance has been beaten every time, but each beat and raise includes acquisitions closed after the guide. Actual / guided midpoint: Q1 2026 50.1M vs 38-40M = 1.29; FY2025 50.7M vs a floor of 36M = 1.41; Q4 2025 30.1M vs a floor of 15M = 2.0 (floors, not midpoints). The FY2026 target went 110M (2025-11) -> 170-180M (2026-01) -> 375M (2026-03) -> 390M (2026-05) -> 525-550M (2026-08), mostly from the perimeter. The ratio therefore overstates organic beats: apply it, if at all, only to the unreported remainder and only on a like-for-like perimeter. The current target is heavily back-end loaded: H2 2026 must be ~404M against H1 133.9M, and Q4 ~256M at the Q3 guide midpoint of 147.5M. GATE/Bron (closed 2026-09-14, management expects ~65M revenue in full-year 2026) came after the August target: whether it is additive or already assumed is not stated (gap).

GAAP profit is not a guide in either direction. H1 2026 net income +271.6M (Q1 +362.8M) comes from a 404.8M non-cash gain on the warrant liability and a 48.8M deconsolidation gain, less a 46.2M VIE acquisition loss. Q2 operating loss was -162.9M, with SBC 69.1M (82% of revenue; H1 SBC 88.8M = 66% of revenue; FY2025 16.0M = 32%), a 19.2M contingent-consideration charge, 18.6M intangible amortization and 4.4M deal costs. Adjusted EBITDA (-50.6M Q2, -10.9M Q1) excludes SBC, and from Q2 also contingent-consideration changes (definition changed). SBC is treated as a cost. Cash burn is real: CFO -137.4M in H1 2026 (-86.1M in Q2), capex 9.1M. Liquidity at 2026-06-30 was 657.9M cash + 726.6M short-term investments (restricted 8.5M excluded). About 452M of cash went to DZYNE (204.1M), Cyberhawk (118.2M) and GATE/Bron (105M + 25M working capital) in Q3, leaving roughly 930M before Q3 operating burn (derived).

Computed on FY2024-FY2025 rows (understand/forensic_result.json). Piotroski 5/8 (mixed; the no-new-shares signal is missing but in fact fails, since shares rose 4.1x). Altman Z'' 2.44 (grey zone; liabilities include a 489M non-cash warrant liability). Beneish M +2.12 ('likely manipulator' zone), driven by SGI 7.05 from acquired growth; the growth-neutral M is -3.28 ('unlikely'). That is a growth artefact to investigate, not an accusation. ROIC: FY2024 -67%; FY2025 invested capital is negative (net cash above equity + debt after the warrant liability), so ROIC is not meaningful. Incremental ROIC is not meaningful. Rule of 40 does not apply.

No return on capital is evidenced yet. The Q2 2026 operating loss annualizes to about -650M, against operating invested capital of about 0.2B (equity 1,570M + debt ~17M - cash and short-term investments 1,384.5M), and most of that capital is acquisition goodwill (661.4M at Q2 plus 493.5M preliminary DZYNE goodwill, 56% of DZYNE's 879M price). Moat: none evidenced against a named competitor. GAAP gross margin of 43% sits between DroneShield (~60%, C-UAS software-rich) and AeroVironment (~26%) / Elbit (~24%). Every small-drone/C-UAS peer is loss-making. The JIATF-401 C-UAS money visible in the sources went to AeroVironment and DroneShield, not to ONDS. GATE's claimed qualification/design-in barrier (>90 weapon systems) is an issuer claim. Returns are expected to fade toward the cost of capital unless a mechanism is shown.

Management delivers on revenue targets, through acquisitions. Profitability promises moved but have not yet been tested: in 2026-03 the targets were product-level profit by Q3 2026, OAS by Q3 2027 and company-wide by Q1 2028. In 2026-08 they became adjusted-EBITDA targets (platform Q4 2026, company-wide Q4 2027), on a basis that excludes SBC. Q2 was flagged in advance as the peak adjusted-EBITDA loss (-50.6M), so that was consistent. SBC in Q2 was elevated by vesting of key-executive awards. Capital allocation is equity-funded M&A: 829.5M of equity raised in FY2025 and 959.1M in January 2026. Acquisitions: DZYNE 879M (77% in stock), Cyberhawk 118.2M cash, GATE/Bron 205M headline plus up to 185M in earn-outs (stock per the 8-K). Management says it 'expects to execute additional acquisitions in 2026'. No buybacks. Regna AI (2026-10-12, 'powered by Palantir', wholly owned, no disclosed revenue or commitment) is a partner logo, not paid adoption.

Shares outstanding: 93.2M (2024-12-31) -> 380.8M (2025-12-31) -> 529.8M (2026-06-30) -> 570.6M (2026-08-11). Known additions since: 10.69M GATE shares (2026-09-14), 45.0M DZYNE shares due 2027-01-04, the 2026-08-28 and 2026-09-23 issuances (counts not read) and up to 185M of GATE earn-out in stock. Potentially dilutive at Q2: 374.1M (warrants 196.3M, including 121.6M at a 28.00 USD strike that is liability-classified and cash-settleable on a change of control; options 27.9M; RSUs 33.2M; contingently issuable 116.8M). Contingent consideration liabilities total 134.1M (17.2M current + 116.9M long-term). Dilution is the main way growth has been paid for.

Warning row only (sets no number): base rates show that firms growing >20% real usually slow to ~8% within five years, and most 'supergrowers' do not sustain growth. ONDS's own evidence of organic growth is a single company-defined pro forma figure (+85% Q2, >30% for FY2026), so any multi-year growth anchor beyond the FY2026 target rests on backlog conversion and new orders that have not yet been verified.

economics.reason: No price cycle drives the unit economics, and there is no peak margin to revert: the company is loss-making, with gross margin falling from mix. Demand rests on multi-year defense budget lines: U.S. Army LUS IDIQ (982M ceiling, ~240M ordered), the 140M CEV program, JIATF-401 C-UAS funding and the Pentagon Drone Dominance program, plus an order book that grows faster than revenue (Q2 book-to-bill 2.1x). The conflict-driven part (Israel 45% of Q2 revenue; Customer A 40%) is carried as a concentration and reversion risk in the bear case, not as a mean-reverting margin cycle. The evidence that ONDS's own organic growth is structural is thin: one company-defined pro forma figure.
